Issued at 332 PM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

===== Clouds Increase with Increasing Rain Chances Sunday =====

Temperatures are on track to reach the mid to upper 70s and isolated 
80 degrees in our southern communities. Skies are clear now with 
winds gusting to 20 MPH at times. After sunset, winds will become 
near calm with high level clouds streaming in overhead. Lows will 
reach the upper 40s to low 50s by sunrise as clouds continue to 
build from moisture streaming in from Texas, and from a slowly 
descending cold front in our north. As this front moves into our 
southern Indiana counties in the early morning, dew points will drop 
and slightly cooler air will move in. This front will be aided by a 
weak high near 700 mb with northerly flow to push it near or along 
the Cumberland Parkway. In the morning, some low to mid level clouds 
will move in across our northern counties and will slowly raise 
higher as they progress to the south by early afternoon. Highs are 
coolest across our north in the low to mid 70s and in the upper 70s 
to near 80 near the TN border. 

Despite this southward push of cooler air, it will be relatively 
short lived as SW flow returns later in the day with continuous 
moisture advection trying to erode away the dry air in place at the 
surface. Lows on Saturday morning will be in the upper 40s to mid 
50s again as overcast skies take hold. What will be going on then is 
the slow retreat of a high to our east while the remnants of what's 
left of TC Vance and a weak wave along the Gulf begin to move 
northwards towards KY late Saturday night into Sunday morning. 
Saturday will remain dry however, as highs remain mild in the mid 
70s in the south and upper 60s across our north. A warm air mass 
will move in late Saturday into Sunday and act as a precursor to the 
moist advection from the remnants of Vance.

Sunday morning, continuous moisture advection from the SW with the 
approaching wave will increase PWATs somewhere in the 1.1-1.4" 
range. Seems now that total rainfall has increased a little, 
considering the recent Euro/CMC guidance. GFS guidance has the most 
robust signal. Considering moisture advection has to overcome PWATs 
near 0.5" along with dry air at the surface, it may take awhile for 
incoming rain to reach the ground, meaning the atmosphere will 
moisten from the top-down. 

The approaching wave will act as an inverted trough on the west side 
of the retreating high and will bring showers, potentially with 
moderate rainfall rates, especially in our SW communities. Since the 
moisture from the Gulf and the remnant energy from Vance has a long 
way to travel and must erode counteractive preexisting conditions 
away, rainfall totals entail a lot of uncertainty. 25-75th 
percentile range anywhere from a trace to just under an inch. So the 
high end of rainfall totals have increased, but the lower end hasn't 
changed since the last update. For now, expect spotty to scattered 
showers Sunday morning through the evening hours, with residual 
drizzle or sprinkles leftover that may last into Monday. Highs range 
in the mid 60s to near 70, with the Bluegrass region remaining the 
warmest coinciding with the lowest rainfall potential. 

===== Anticipating Busy Pattern Next Week =====

Residual moisture with southerly flow remaining Monday will keep 
cloud cover around and the occasional shower or sprinkle in the 
afternoon. Highs will be in the upper 60s to low 70s as well, with 
little change in the weather during the day. As the week progresses, 
a deep trough will be moving east through the Rockies and slowly 
approach the Ohio Valley. Within this trough, the Pacific 
subtropical jet will be feeding moisture to the expectant developing 
low within the trough as it moves east of the Rockies. This low will 
be cut off from the polar jet and without strong steering flow, will 
progress eastwards slowly and potentially meander through the 
Plains. Right now, the best timing for our next rainfall seems to be 
on Wednesday, possibly as late as the overnight hours into Thursday. 
This incoming low has a greater potential to dump more rain on us 
with increasing PWATs and greater moisture feed from the 
Pacific/Gulf, although probabilities of our CWA receiving more than 
an inch of rain Wednesday only reaches a maximum of 25% in our 
southwest. For now, just know that PoPs increase again by middle of 
the week.
